assumptions: Competitor has a public listing on the declared review platform (G2, Capterra, Trustpilot, GetApp, Software Advice, or Product Hunt).
At most 30 reviews fetched from the first page of the platform listing.
Safe project context bounded to at most 8000 bytes from non-sensitive documentation (e.g. README, public docs).
Agent uses web search to locate the competitor listing; does not require the user to paste review text.
cost_drivers: Bounded Codex procedure session using standard rate card; spending capped at configured sandbox ceiling.
Web search calls are gated by the sandbox egress fence (fenced egress, isolated profile).
Execution work scales with number of reviews collected (up to 30) and output narrative size.
Zero paid external integrations or live provider API keys required.
effects: Writes reports/COMPETITOR_REVIEW_MINER.md in the bound project workspace.
No mutations outside reports/COMPETITOR_REVIEW_MINER.md, no secret access, no publication.
Web search is bounded to the declared platform domain.

cases.description: Normal case: well-known competitor on G2 with pain points, loved features, and a switching trigger expected.
Boundary case: same competitor searched on Capterra instead of G2.
Unusable result case: obscure competitor name with no listing on the platform produces a diagnostic report.

rubric.question: Is every pain point, loved feature, and switching trigger backed by verbatim or clearly attributed quotes from reviews found on the declared platform?
Do the three growth opportunities offer concrete, testable positioning, copy, or roadmap actions rather than generic advice?
Does the workflow respect data bounds (cap at 30 reviews, only the declared platform domain, diagnostic output when no listing is found, no sensitive file reads) without hallucinations?
